title: Maybe the First
goal: The first character of a string that might be empty. Say 'maybe' in the type.
hints: chars().next() already IS an Option - the honest signature just passes it along.
unwrap() promises 'never empty'. The second test call disagrees.
explanation: The iterator already answers honestly: next() returns Option<char> because a stream can end. Returning that Option keeps the signature truthful and both tests happy. The unwrap variant claims a char always exists - the type checker then rejects comparing char with Some('h'), and even without that, first_char("") would panic at runtime. When the data can be absent, the type should say so.
